PIZENSY was evaluated in a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, multicenter clinical study in adult patients with symptoms of CIC (NCT02819297).
Phase 3 Study BLI400-302 compared 20 g lactitol (N=299) once daily to placebo (N=304) in a 6 month treatment period.

design.text: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial; lactitol 20 g once daily vs placebo over a 6-month treatment period.

citations.quote: PIZENSY was evaluated in a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, multicenter clinical study in adult patients with symptoms of CIC (NCT02819297). PIZENSY (20 grams once daily) was compared to placebo in a 6-month treatment period.

population.text: Adults with chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC) meeting modified Rome II criteria with an average <3 CSBMs per week; mean age 52 years, 76% female.

citations.quote: Patients were eligible for enrollment if they had an average <3 complete spontaneous bowel movements (CSBMs) per week during the 14 day screening period and met an adapted ROME II definition for a diagnosis of CIC
Patients had a mean age of 52 years (range 18 to 88 years); 76% were female, 60% were white, and 31% were black.

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint: proportion of responders, where a responder had at least 3 CSBMs and an increase of at least 1 CSBM from baseline in the same week for at least 9 of the first 12 weeks and at least 3 of the last 4 weeks (Weeks 9-12).

citations.quote: A responder was defined as a patient who had at least 3 CSBMs in a given week and an increase of at least 1 CSBM from baseline in the same week for at least 9 weeks out of the first 12-week treatment period and at least 3 of the last 4 weeks (Weeks 9-12).

result.text: Responder rate 25% with lactitol vs 13% with placebo (treatment difference 12%; 95% CI 6.0, 18.5), statistically significant.

citations.quote: The efficacy responder rates for the primary endpoint were 25% in the lactitol arm and 13% in the placebo arm (12% treatment difference; 95% CI: 6.0 - 18.5).

indication.text: PIZENSY is an osmotic laxative indicated for the treatment of chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC) in adults.

target_moa.text: Lactitol is an osmotic laxative; following oral administration it causes the influx of water into the small intestine, leading to a laxative effect in the colon.

citations.quote: Lactitol is an osmotic laxative that causes the influx of water into the small intestine leading to a laxative effect in the colon.

modality.text: Small molecule (synthetic polyol sugar / synthetic derivative of lactose)

citations.quote: Lactitol, an osmotic laxative, is a new chemical entity that is a synthetic derivative of lactose, and consists of galactose and sorbitol linked through a glycoside bond.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=3%) were upper respiratory tract infection (9% vs 6% placebo), flatulence (8% vs 3%), diarrhea (4% vs 3%), increased blood creatinine phosphokinase (4% vs 3%), abdominal distension (3% vs 1%), and increased blood pressure (3% vs 1%). Severe diarrhea was reported in 2 (1%) PIZENSY-treated patients vs none on placebo.
